Subject-Aware Multimodal Glucose Forecasting with Channel-Temporal Attention and Iterative Residual Refinement

Abstract:

Diabetes Mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorderthat requires continuous monitoring and accurate glucose level prediction to prevent hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia. Existing algorithms typically depend solely on Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) signals and often fail to capture multimodal physiological dynamics and inter-subject variability. This paper presents a multimodal deep learning framework for personalized multi-horizon blood glucose prediction using physiological and physical activity data from the OhioT1DM dataset. The proposed CNN-BiGRU framework, which incorporates Squeezeand-Excitation attention, temporal attention pooling, and subject embedding, combines heart rate, physical activity, glucose dynamics, rolling statistical descriptors and temporal encoding for multi-horizon glucose forecasting. Experimental results show strong performance in 5, 15 and 30 minute horizons with a MARD of 4.6052% and a Clarke Error Grid Zone A accuracy of 98.09% for the 5-minute horizon and MARD of 8.4711% and a Zone A accuracy of 92.01% at the 15-minute horizon. The framework also demonstrated stable forecasting behavior for longer prediction horizons while preserving computational efficiency. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining physiological signals with physical activity data for reliable realtime glucose prediction in closed-loop diabetes management systems. Keywords—Glucose forecasting, Multimodal physiological signals, Temporal attention, Personalized healthcare
